tasks.short: Assess business processes, identify fraud exposure, and agree priorities for stronger controls.

steps.what: Collect transaction extracts, control records, and previous findings.
Read procedures and document apparent control gaps.

loop.input: Approved process procedures, control records, and previous findings.
loop.output: Draft control findings with source passages and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Verify citations and distinguish documented controls from evidence of their operation.
loop.stop: Two passes per procedure; unresolved or contradictory passages go to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedures describe responsibilities and exceptions in varied prose.

steps.what: Discuss actual practices, workarounds, and possible abuse with process owners.
Assess fraud scenarios, control effectiveness, and residual exposure.
Challenge ratings and approve remediation priorities.
Record approved ratings, assign actions, and schedule follow-up.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration brings authorised records from {ERP}, {EXPENSE}, and {PROCUREMENT} into {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliation checks and a {BI} view. A bounded reading loop drafts source-linked control findings from {DOCS}; analysts assess exposure, risk owners approve priorities, and {WORKFLOW} updates the register and {PROJECT} actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across systems, procedures rarely match actual practice, and risk ratings require contextual judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes connectors, reconciliation checks, and register interfaces cheaper to build. Bounded text extraction reduces procedure-reading effort without replacing risk assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden workarounds, collusion, incomplete records, and estimating losses remain difficult. Employee-level analysis needs a lawful basis, proportionate access, and consultation under applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising how incentives, authority, and informal practices create opportunities that transaction rules miss.

ambition.what: Monthly reprioritisation of fraud-control testing using refreshed exposure evidence.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling packs and more time investigating emerging exposure. They can propose testing priorities monthly; risk acceptance remains with the risk owner.

reach.task: Develop operational loss scenarios for a business process.
reach.learn: Scenario calibration, uncertainty ranges, and risk appetite thresholds.

evidence.claim: Rules and machine learning can support monitoring with reasons per alert and human review; this supports evidence preparation, not automated business-risk acceptance.
Linked evidence can reduce checking effort: Baker Tilly Netherlands reported statement checking falling from eight to two hours. This vendor case does not measure fraud-risk assessment.
In the Netherlands, employee behaviour monitoring can require works council consent; requirements elsewhere depend on national rules.
GDPR purpose limitation, access controls, and retention requirements apply to personal data used in fraud assessment.

assumptions: The baseline is a periodic assessment in a mid-size company, with transaction systems and a manually maintained risk register.
Judgement covers less than half the work through explicit rules; preparation is more automatable than the final assessment.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for one process family and a limited connector set.
unknowns: Which transaction sources, identifiers, and export interfaces are available?
Who can approve risk ratings and accept residual risk?
Does the intended analysis monitor employees, and what consultation is required?
research_questions: Which control gaps predict confirmed losses rather than merely unusual activity?
How well do documented controls match observed practice?
new_work: Review source-linked findings and unresolved contradictions.
Investigate missing records and failed reconciliation checks.
Maintain mappings, access permissions, and risk-rating definitions.

tasks.short: Recommend practical improvements to fraud detection and agree how process owners will implement them.

steps.what: Compile current controls, alert outcomes, and previous recommendations.
Select improvements against fraud exposure, workload, and operational constraints.
Write recommendations with rationale, implementation steps, and success measures.

loop.input: Selected recommendations, baseline evidence, and an approved brief template.
loop.output: Recommendation brief with evidence references and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Recalculate figures deterministically; examiner checks feasibility, citations, and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence is marked for the examiner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining case-specific trade-offs and operational changes requires tailored prose.

steps.what: Discuss trade-offs and approve changes, owners, and delivery dates.
Enter agreed actions and arrange progress reviews.

tasks.design: A read-only integration assembles a detection baseline from {ERP}, {DOCS}, and {PROJECT}, with deterministic outcome metrics. After the examiner selects recommendations, a bounded loop drafts the brief in {DOCS}; approved actions flow through {WORKFLOW} into {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recommendations depend on fragmented outcomes, local operating constraints, and persuasive explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable metrics, cheaper integrations, and source-grounded drafting reduce preparation and follow-up effort.
tasks.still_hard: Proving detection effectiveness is difficult when undetected fraud is unknown. Operational resistance, customer friction, employee monitoring, and budget trade-offs need human negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing interventions people can operate and gaining agreement without treating every anomaly as wrongdoing.

ambition.what: Quarterly fraud-control design clinic for smaller internal departments.

tasks.altitude: The examiner can spend more of the week advising process owners and checking whether changes worked. They gain capacity to facilitate design trials; spending and control approval stay with existing owners.

reach.task: Build the investment case for a control improvement.
reach.learn: Cost estimation, expected-loss ranges, and operational benefit measurement.

evidence.claim: Monitoring technology supports rules, model signals, and reasons per alert; selecting business interventions remains a separate advisory decision.
Moody's Credit Memo demonstrates evidence-based financial memo drafting, an adjacent capability rather than a documented fraud-advisory outcome.
Employee monitoring changes can require consultation under national rules; the Netherlands provides an explicit works council consent example.

assumptions: This is internal advice; external advisory work adds client confidentiality and engagement arrangements.
The automation prior overstates replacement because recommendation selection and agreement remain substantial human work.
Build ranges cover advisory preparation and action tracking, not implementation of new detection controls.
unknowns: Are alert outcomes reliable enough to distinguish confirmed cases, false positives, and unresolved alerts?
Who approves control changes and associated spending?
Which departments currently lack access to fraud-control advice?
research_questions: Which success measures capture prevented loss without rewarding excessive alerts?
Which recurring recommendations can use a fixed template without losing important context?
new_work: Review drafted rationale and check evidence references.
Maintain recommendation templates and baseline metric definitions.
Follow up on action outcomes and unexpected operational costs.

tasks.short: Compare fraud-detection technologies through evidence review, controlled trials, and adoption recommendations.

steps.what: Define detection needs, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Review technical documentation and research websites using the {OTHER} browser.

loop.input: A fixed set of technical documents and evaluation criteria.
loop.output: Comparison table with quoted support, dates, and unverified claims.
loop.check: Verify citations and distinguish claimed features from independently tested capabilities.
loop.stop: Twenty documents and two extraction passes; unresolved claims remain unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Capabilities and limitations are described inconsistently in prose.

steps.what: Prepare permitted historical records and confirmed outcomes for a controlled trial.
Run fixed trial scenarios in the {OTHER} fraud-detection test environment.
Calculate detection results, review workload, and trial costs.
Interpret limitations and recommend adoption, further testing, or rejection.
Approve the next evaluation stage or adoption proposal.

tasks.design: A bounded document-reading loop creates a cited comparison in {DOCS}. Deterministic jobs in {DATA_PLATFORM} prepare permitted test data, run fixed trials through {OTHER} test interfaces, and publish reproducible metrics in {BI}; analysts interpret results and sponsors approve next steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each comparison rebuilds datasets and metrics, while technical claims use incompatible definitions.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building reusable trial adapters and scoring scripts. Bounded extraction makes source comparison faster.
tasks.still_hard: Confirmed fraud labels are incomplete, historical cases can leak into training data, and attackers change behaviour. Restricted test interfaces and lawful access to representative data can dominate cost.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether measured gains survive real workloads, adversarial adaptation, and the company's operating constraints.

ambition.what: Quarterly evidence-based decisions on whether a detection challenger deserves a shadow trial.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding comparisons and more time challenging evaluation quality. They can initiate repeatable comparisons within an agreed sandbox; procurement and deployment decisions remain with the sponsor.

reach.task: Evaluate a detection challenger against an existing baseline.
reach.learn: Temporal holdouts, label leakage, precision-recall trade-offs, and drift measurement.

evidence.claim: Hawk documents rules and machine learning for transaction monitoring, providing a concrete technology category to evaluate.
The digest's spreadsheet-agent benchmark reports a material numerical error, supporting independent deterministic tie-outs.
The EU AI Act's natural-person creditworthiness category excepts fraud detection; that exception does not settle classification of other intended uses.
Representative holdout testing and incomplete fraud labels limit conclusions drawn from historical trials.

assumptions: Trials run in an approved sandbox with no automatic changes to live alerts or individual decisions.
The first build compares two candidates using one transaction domain and fixed evaluation criteria.
Time shares reflect an evaluation with a practical trial, rather than a literature-only review.
Existing access approval covers the permitted internal test dataset; new disclosures require separate approval.
unknowns: Which candidates offer usable test interfaces and trial rights?
How reliable and representative are confirmed fraud labels?
What data transfers, employee consultation, and access approvals would each trial require?
Who owns the deployment and purchasing decision?
research_questions: Can the trial distinguish better detection from increased investigator workload?
How does performance change on later periods and previously unseen fraud patterns?
Which simpler configured rules match the candidate's measured benefit?
new_work: Maintain trial adapters, benchmark versions, and reproducibility records.
Review extracted claims against original documentation.
Investigate metric anomalies, data leakage, and unreliable outcome labels.
Refresh evaluation criteria when fraud patterns or operating costs change.

tasks.short: Gather case evidence through authorised field observation and produce a defensible factual record.

steps.what: Assess the case purpose, necessity, permitted scope, and legal constraints.
Approve the field operation after required legal consultation.
Prepare the assignment pack, observation forms, and evidence identifiers.
Observe within the approved mandate and record contemporaneous facts.
Upload originals and register evidence provenance, access, and custody.
Write and sign the factual field report with evidence references.

loop.input: Field notes and verified evidence-register entries.
loop.output: Draft factual chronology with source references and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Investigator checks every assertion against originals and separates observation from interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous passages remain for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need careful consolidation; fixed fields cannot capture every observation.

tasks.design: A restricted case workspace in {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} generates assignment packs only from approved mandates and records evidence identifiers, hashes, and custody events. Field observation remains human; a bounded loop drafts a source-linked chronology for investigator verification and signature.
tasks.previous_blocker: The core activity requires physical presence and situational judgement. Preparation and evidence handling often lack consistent templates and connected records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured access controls, deterministic evidence registration, and cheaper form generation improve paperwork. Bounded drafting helps consolidate notes without claiming to automate observation.
tasks.still_hard: Lawful authority, necessity, admissibility, physical conditions, and reliable identification remain case-specific. GDPR and national rules on surveillance, recording, and employment constrain what may be collected and retained.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing context, distinguishing observation from inference, and stopping when conditions exceed the authorised mandate.
tasks.altitude: The investigator saves some preparation and reporting time, while fieldwork still dominates the week. No additional surveillance or case-disposal decision rights are gained.

reach.task: Review whether a proposed evidence-collection method is permitted.
reach.learn: Purpose limitation, proportionality, retention requirements, and applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Field observation and interpretation remain human activities; records tooling can support preparation and custody documentation.
GDPR applies to personal data collected during investigations; surveillance and evidential requirements also depend on national rules.
The Netherlands provides an explicit consent requirement for arrangements monitoring employee behaviour; it does not establish permission for a particular surveillance operation.
The digest's fraud-list enforcement example illustrates the consequences of unlawful personal-data processing, rather than evidence that surveillance can be automated.

assumptions: Field surveillance is occasional in a mid-size company and may be assigned to a qualified external investigator.
The baseline covers an authorised operation, with travel and waiting included in field time.
The mandate approval authorises the field action; work outside its scope returns for a new decision.
Evidence files are preserved before registration review; review confirms metadata and custody assertions.
Build ranges cover supporting records and paperwork, not new surveillance equipment or collection powers.
unknowns: Is field surveillance part of the organisation's legitimate investigation remit?
Which national rules, professional qualifications, and consultation requirements apply?
What custody, retention, and evidential standards must the case meet?
Can the existing document store preserve originals, access logs, and retention restrictions?
research_questions: Which registration controls best expose missing custody events or altered files?
Does assisted chronology drafting save time after full factual verification?
new_work: Verify evidence metadata and resolve missing custody information.
Check drafted chronology against original notes and recordings.
Maintain mandate templates, access permissions, and retention schedules.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward risk interpretation, control design, and rigorous testing as evidence assembly and paperwork shrink. Investigative conversations, field observation, risk acceptance, and consequential case decisions retain their human owners.
reach: Support financial risk specialists with evidence-based operational loss scenarios.
Help financial managers assess control investments.
Work with data scientists on reproducible detection evaluations.
Support compliance officers with documented evidence-collection proposals.
skills_to_grow: Detection metrics, incomplete labels, and controlled evaluation.
GDPR, applicable EU AI Act requirements, and national investigation rules.
Evidence custody and critical review of generated prose.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring fraud-control assurance service that refreshes exposure assessments, tests detection challengers, and measures remediation outcomes while keeping consequential decisions with accountable people.
